\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{حطاب} (ḥaṭṭāb)}{حطاب (ḥaṭṭāb)}]{\ar{حطاب} (ḥaṭṭāb) — a woodcutter}

\label{lesson:AR-C344-hattab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a coincidence, then the Arabic for to take a risk.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{حطاب}}
\textbf{\ar{حطاب}} — \emph{ḥaṭṭāb} — \textquotedblleft{}a woodcutter\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كان} \ar{في} \ar{الغابة} \ar{حطاب} \ar{فقير}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāna fī al-ghāba ḥaṭṭāb faqīr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There was a poor woodcutter in the forest.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{حطاب}} (\emph{ḥaṭṭāb}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-ṭ-b} (Lane), where \emph{ḥaṭab} is firewood. The \emph{faʿʿāl} pattern names the trade: \textquotedblleft{}the firewood man\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥaṭṭāb}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥaṭṭāb}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāna fī al-ghāba ḥaṭṭāb faqīr.} — There was a poor woodcutter in the forest.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a coincidence, then the Arabic for to take a risk, then say \emph{ḥaṭṭāb} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{حطاب} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A woodcutter\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{سحر} (saḥara)}{سحر (saḥara)}]{\ar{سحر} (saḥara) — to enchant, to bewitch}

\label{lesson:AR-C344-sahara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to take a risk, then the Arabic for a woodcutter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{سحر}}
\textbf{\ar{سحر}} — \emph{saḥara} — \textquotedblleft{}to enchant, to bewitch\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{سحرت} \ar{الموسيقى} \ar{الجمهور}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{saḥarat al-mūsīqā al-jumhūr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The music enchanted the audience.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يسحر}, \emph{yasḥar}.

The noun \ar{سحر}, \emph{siḥr}, magic, is spelled the same.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{سحر}} (\emph{saḥara}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-ḥ-r} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to enchant\textquotedblright{}; \emph{siḥr} is magic, and \emph{saḥar}, the time before dawn, is spelled the same.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saḥara}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saḥara}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{saḥarat al-mūsīqā al-jumhūr.} — The music enchanted the audience.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to take a risk, then the Arabic for a woodcutter, then say \emph{saḥara} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{سحر} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To enchant, to bewitch\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تحول} (taḥawwala)}{تحول (taḥawwala)}]{\ar{تحول} (taḥawwala) — to turn into, to change}

\label{lesson:AR-C344-tahawwala}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a woodcutter, then the Arabic for to enchant.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تحول}}
\textbf{\ar{تحول}} — \emph{taḥawwala} — \textquotedblleft{}to turn into, to change\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تحول} \ar{الضفدع} \ar{إلى} \ar{أمير}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taḥawwala aḍ-ḍifdaʿ ilā amīr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The frog turned into a prince.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتحول}, \emph{yataḥawwal}.

It takes \ar{إلى}: \ar{تحول} \ar{إلى}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تحول}} (\emph{taḥawwala}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-w-l} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to change, to shift\textquotedblright{}, the root of \emph{ḥāl}, a state. It is Form V, \textquotedblleft{}to change oneself\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taḥawwala}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taḥawwala}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taḥawwala aḍ-ḍifdaʿ ilā amīr.} — The frog turned into a prince.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a woodcutter, then the Arabic for to enchant, then say \emph{taḥawwala} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تحول} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To turn into, to change\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تحقق} (taḥaqqaqa)}{تحقق (taḥaqqaqa)}]{\ar{تحقق} (taḥaqqaqa) — to come true; to make sure}

\label{lesson:AR-C344-tahaqqaqa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to enchant, then the Arabic for to turn into.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تحقق}}
\textbf{\ar{تحقق}} — \emph{taḥaqqaqa} — \textquotedblleft{}to come true; to make sure\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تحققت} \ar{أمنية} \ar{البنت} \ar{الصغيرة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taḥaqqaqat umniyyat al-bint aṣ-ṣaghīra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The little girl’s wish came true.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتحقق}, \emph{yataḥaqqaq}.

\ar{تحقق} \ar{من}: to check: \ar{تحقق} \ar{من} \ar{الموعد}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تحقق}} (\emph{taḥaqqaqa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-q-q} (Lane), the root of \emph{ḥaqq}, truth. It is Form V, \textquotedblleft{}to become true\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taḥaqqaqa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taḥaqqaqa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taḥaqqaqat umniyyat al-bint aṣ-ṣaghīra.} — The little girl’s wish came true.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to enchant, then the Arabic for to turn into, then say \emph{taḥaqqaqa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تحقق} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To come true; to make sure\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{انتقم} (intaqama)}{انتقم (intaqama)}]{\ar{انتقم} (intaqama) — to take revenge}

\label{lesson:AR-C344-intaqama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to turn into, then the Arabic for to come true.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{انتقم}}
\textbf{\ar{انتقم}} — \emph{intaqama} — \textquotedblleft{}to take revenge\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{انتقم} \ar{البطل} \ar{من} \ar{الساحر} \ar{الشرير}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{intaqama al-baṭal min as-sāḥir ash-shirrīr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The hero took revenge on the wicked magician.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{ينتقم}, \emph{yantaqim}.

It takes \ar{من}: \ar{انتقم} \ar{من}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{انتقم}} (\emph{intaqama}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-q-m} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to take vengeance, to punish\textquotedblright{}. It is Form VIII, \textquotedblleft{}to punish for oneself\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{intaqama}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{intaqama}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{intaqama al-baṭal min as-sāḥir ash-shirrīr.} — The hero took revenge on the wicked magician.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to turn into, then the Arabic for to come true, then say \emph{intaqama} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
